Second, we show how the BVP for the splitting probability of $M$ Brownian particles can be mapped onto the $M$th order moment equation of a stochastic diffusion equation with resetting. We thus establish a general mathematical framework to study exit problems for globally-driven particle systems.

AI.tldr: This paper extends exit statistics for multiple Brownian particles under global stochastic resetting in an interval with absorbing boundaries, deriving nested BVPs for joint splitting probabilities and mapping them to moment equations of a stochastic diffusion equation.
AI.motivation: There is growing interest in statistical correlations emerging among non-interacting Brownian particles subject to common fluctuating environments (e.g., global resetting, switching potentials, fluctuating diffusivities). Prior work focused on stationary joint densities; this paper aims to understand exit statistics and pairwise correlations in such globally-driven systems.
AI.method: (1) Generalizes Itô's lemma to derive a hierarchy of nested boundary value problems (BVPs) for joint splitting probabilities that all M particles exit from the same end. (2) Explicitly solves the BVP for M=2 to illustrate pairwise correlations. (3) Maps the BVP for M particles onto the M-th order moment equation of a stochastic diffusion equation with resetting.
AI.result: Explicit solution for the joint splitting probability for a pair of Brownian particles (M=2) under global resetting, demonstrating the emergence of pairwise correlations. A general mathematical framework connecting the multi-particle exit problem to moment equations of a stochastic diffusion equation with resetting is established.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a general mathematical framework for studying exit problems in globally-driven particle systems, showing that multi-particle splitting probabilities map onto higher-order moment equations of a stochastic diffusion equation, enabling analytical treatment of correlations induced by the common fluctuating environment.

title: Probing Dielectric Screening in van der Waals Heterostructures via Pressure-Tuned Exciton Rydberg Series
summary: Excitons in two-dimensional semiconductors are directly exposed to the environment and are sensitive to the dielectric properties of their surrounding. Here, we show that the Rydberg series of excited states of excitons in a monolayer WSe$_2$ encapsulated in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) can be used to probe the pressure-induced modifications of the surrounding dielectric properties. We propose a model based on the pressure induced evolution of the interlayer distances in this van der Waals heterostructure and on the bulk dielectric properties of hBN. This approach allows a direct measurement of the dielectric constant of pressurized hBN and establishes a new methodology for dielectric sensing.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates that exciton Rydberg states in monolayer WSe2 encapsulated in hBN can probe pressure-induced changes in the dielectric environment, enabling direct measurement of hBN's dielectric constant under pressure and establishing a new dielectric sensing methodology.
AI.motivation: To exploit the environmental sensitivity of excitons in 2D semiconductors for probing pressure-induced modifications of dielectric properties in the surrounding hBN.
AI.method: Using the Rydberg series of excited exciton states in monolayer WSe2 encapsulated in hBN, combined with a model based on pressure-induced evolution of interlayer distances in the van der Waals heterostructure and bulk dielectric properties of hBN.
AI.result: Direct measurement of the dielectric constant of pressurized hBN.
AI.conclusion: The approach establishes a new methodology for dielectric sensing.

title: Finite-width adiabatic shear banding and dislocation patterning in mesoscale polycrystalline aggregates
summary: Dynamic shear banding under adiabatic conditions in a mesoscale polycrystalline aggregate is studied using a model of mesoscale dislocation mechanics and experiments. The model involves a length scale related to hardening induced by excess/polar/geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density, and utilizes a simple classical crystal plasticity model with isotropic Voce law hardening. Simulations of statistically representative volume elements of a polycrystal determined from experimental samples are conducted. Studies in 2-d (section) and 3-d capture the experimentally observed finite-width shear bands and the formation of low-angle subgrain boundaries even in the absence of heat conduction in the model, as well as size-dependent strengthening for grain sizes from 1 to 20 $μ$m. The 2-d and large-scale 3-d simulations, the latter involving 1 million finite elements, provide access to the progressive evolution of material strength, stress state, and temperature in the course of large deformations. GND distributions accumulate at grain boundaries and form patterned structures within grain interiors, offering insight into the microstructural changes that precede failure in adiabatic shear bands. Mesh-converged, delocalized and localized plastic flow to very large deformations without softening is observed for a significant range of parameters, reflecting a competition between GND hardening and thermal softening in setting the non-softening steady state in the absence of other ductile damage mechanisms in the model.

AI.tldr: This paper uses a mesoscale dislocation mechanics model and experiments to study dynamic shear banding in polycrystalline aggregates under adiabatic conditions, revealing how geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) hardening and thermal softening compete to produce finite-width shear bands and low-angle subgrain boundaries without heat conduction, with simulations up to 1 million elements showing size-dependent strengthening from 1–20 μm grain sizes.
AI.motivation: To understand the microstructural mechanisms underlying adiabatic shear band formation and failure in polycrystalline metals, particularly the roles of GND-induced hardening and thermal softening, using both modeling and experimental validation.
AI.method: A mesoscale dislocation mechanics model incorporating a length scale from GND-density-induced hardening, combined with classical crystal plasticity and isotropic Voce law hardening. 2-D and 3-D FE simulations of statistically representative volume elements of polycrystals (up to 1 million elements), validated against experiments.
AI.result: Finite-width shear bands and low-angle subgrain boundaries form even without heat conduction; GNDs accumulate at grain boundaries and form patterned structures; size-dependent strengthening observed for grain sizes 1–20 μm; mesh-converged, delocalized and localized plastic flow to large deformations without softening occurs over a significant parameter range.
AI.conclusion: The competition between GND hardening and thermal softening governs the non-softening steady state in adiabatic shear banding, offering insight into microstructural changes preceding failure, even when ductile damage mechanisms are absent.

title: Quantum Mpemba effect for operators in open systems
summary: The quantum Mpemba effect concerns with anomalous relaxation of quantum states that evolves either under unitary or non-unitary dynamics. In the context of open quantum systems, while most studies focus on quantum states evolving under completely positive trace-presing dynamics described by the Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equation, we demonstrate that an analogous effect can arise at the level of operators. In particular, we show that operators that evolves under the adjoint Liouvillian -- despite not being a trace-preserving map -- can still exhibit a genuine Mpemba effect. We derive general conditions under which this phenomenon can occur and validate our predictions for three different open quantum setups. Our results broaden the scope of the Mpemba effect in quantum systems and provide a framework for controlling the relaxation of physically relevant observables.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates that the quantum Mpemba effect, previously studied for quantum states, can also occur at the operator level under adjoint Liouvillian dynamics, deriving general conditions and validating predictions across three open quantum systems.
AI.motivation: To broaden the scope of the quantum Mpemba effect by showing it can arise not only in quantum state evolution but also at the operator level under adjoint Liouvillian dynamics, which is not a trace-preserving map.
AI.method: Derivation of general conditions for the operator-level Mpemba effect under adjoint Liouvillian evolution, validated through three distinct open quantum setups.
AI.result: Operators evolving under the adjoint Liouvillian can exhibit a genuine Mpemba effect despite not being trace-preserving; general conditions for this phenomenon are identified and experimentally verified in three different systems.
AI.conclusion: The findings expand the understanding of the Mpemba effect in quantum systems and establish a framework for controlling relaxation dynamics of physically relevant observables.

title: Effect of electric current on optical response of viscous electron-hole plasma
summary: The influence of the Hall voltage on the photoluminescence of a dense hydrodynamic electron-hole plasma laser generated in a mesoscopic n-doped GaAs channel under intense laser excitation is studied. Laser excitation induces an interband current determined by the recombination of photogenerated electron-hole pairs. As a result, background electrons drifting under the influence of the Hall voltage form an effective Hall current. The Coulomb drag caused by the Hall current causes the accumulation of light holes, leading to the appearance of a double photoluminescence line formed by the recombination of excitons and trions. In contrast, in the absence of a Hall current, the shift in the photoluminescence energy associated with heavy holes occurs due to the electric field created by the Hall potential difference.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how Hall voltage affects photoluminescence in a dense electron-hole plasma in n-doped GaAs under laser excitation, revealing Hall-current-induced double PL lines from excitons/trions and field-induced heavy-hole energy shifts.
AI.motivation: To understand the influence of the Hall voltage on photoluminescence properties of a dense hydrodynamic electron-hole plasma in a mesoscopic n-doped GaAs channel under intense laser excitation.
AI.method: Laser excitation generates an interband current via recombination of photogenerated electron-hole pairs; background electrons drift under the Hall voltage forming an effective Hall current; Coulomb drag from the Hall current causes light-hole accumulation.
AI.result: A double photoluminescence line appears from exciton and trion recombination due to Hall-current-induced light-hole accumulation; in the absence of Hall current, a heavy-hole photoluminescence energy shift occurs due to the Hall potential difference electric field.
AI.conclusion: Hall voltage induces distinct photoluminescence signatures (double lines from light holes, energy shifts from heavy holes) via Hall current drag and Hall electric field effects in dense electron-hole plasmas.

title: Ferroelectric polarization controlled orbital Hall conductivity in a higher-order topological insulator: \textit{d1T}-phase monolayer MoS$_2$
summary: The higher-order topological insulator is an extended concept of the conventional topological insulator, which obeys the generalization of the standard bulk-boundary correspondence. In our paper, we predict the monolayer \textit{d1T}-phase transition metal dichalcogenide MoS$_2$ to be a higher-order topological insulator, while also possessing intriguing ferroelectric characteristics. We explicitly demonstrate the nontrivial topological index and reveal the hallmark corner states with quantized fractional charge within the bulk band gap. Second, we show the existence of a nonzero orbital Hall conductivity plateau within the energy gap which is a signature to identify higher-order topology system. Additionally, we investigate the relationship between the ferroelectricity and the orbital Hall conductivity of \textit{d1T} MoS$_2$ and find that the direction of ferroelectric polarization can modulate the positive and negative values of the orbital Hall conductivity $σ_{\rm{OH}}^x$. Our findings provide the theory and material candidate for ferroelectricity tunable orbital Hall effect which is promising to realize the external electric field controllable orbitronics.

AI.tldr: The paper predicts monolayer d1T-MoS₂ as a higher-order topological insulator with ferroelectricity, demonstrating corner states, quantized fractional charge, and a nonzero orbital Hall conductivity plateau that can be modulated by ferroelectric polarization direction.
AI.motivation: To extend the concept of higher-order topological insulators to monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides and explore the interplay between topological properties and ferroelectricity, aiming to realize electric-field-controllable orbitronics.
AI.method: First-principles calculations and theoretical analysis to demonstrate nontrivial topological indices, corner states with quantized fractional charge, orbital Hall conductivity plateaus, and the modulation of orbital Hall conductivity by ferroelectric polarization in monolayer d1T-MoS₂.
AI.result: Monolayer d1T-MoS₂ is identified as a higher-order topological insulator with ferroelectric properties; it exhibits hallmark corner states and a nonzero orbital Hall conductivity plateau; ferroelectric polarization direction can switch the sign of orbital Hall conductivity σ_{OH}^x.
AI.conclusion: The findings provide both the theoretical framework and a material candidate for ferroelectricity-tunable orbital Hall effect, enabling external electric field control of orbitronic devices.

title: Entropy additivity from exponential decay of correlations: a coarse-grained operator approach
summary: Thermodynamic extensivity is commonly introduced as a postulate -- the homogeneity of degree one in thermodynamic potentials. We provide a constructive derivation of this property from microscopic conditions on the pair potential, without assuming it. Working with the one- and two-particle reduced densities of the $N$-body canonical Gibbs state, we introduce a combined coarse-graining operator $\mathcal{C}$ on single-particle phase space $\mathcal{M}=Λ\times\mathbb{R}^3$, producing dimensionless mesoscopic probabilities over spatial--momentum cells $\{V_i\timesΠ_α\}$. Under three conditions on the pair potential -- stability, temperedness, and exponential cluster decomposition with correlation length $ξ$ -- we show, using the Ursell cluster expansion, that the coarse-grained entropy satisfies \[S_{\mathrm{CG}}=\sum_i S_i+O\!\left(\frac{|Λ|}{\ell^d}e^{-\ell/ξ}\right),\] where $\ell\ggξ$ is the cell diameter. The correction is exponentially suppressed per cell, making entropy additive and recovering the thermodynamic limit of Ruelle and Fisher in explicit operator language. For systems with long-range interactions, where temperedness fails, the correction does not vanish, and non-additivity is quantified through inter-cell mutual information. We further show that spatial averaging does not commute with nonlinear thermodynamic functionals such as the entropy density -- a thermodynamic analogue of the cosmological averaging problem -- and we derive the generalised Euler relation with explicit surface corrections.

AI.tldr: This paper derives thermodynamic extensivity (homogeneity of degree one) from microscopic pair potential conditions—stability, temperedness, and exponential cluster decomposition—using the Ursell cluster expansion, showing that coarse-grained entropy is additive with exponentially suppressed corrections. For long-range interactions, non-additivity is quantified via mutual information, and the paper also addresses non-commutation of spatial averaging with entropy density, deriving a generalized Euler relation with surface corrections.
AI.motivation: To provide a constructive, microscopic derivation of thermodynamic extensivity (typically taken as a postulate) from conditions on the pair potential, bridging statistical mechanics and thermodynamics without assuming homogeneity a priori.
AI.method: The authors work with one- and two-particle reduced densities of the N-body canonical Gibbs state, introduce a coarse-graining operator C on single-particle phase space, partition space-momentum into cells, and apply the Ursell cluster expansion under three conditions: stability, temperedness, and exponential cluster decomposition with correlation length ξ.
AI.result: The coarse-grained entropy satisfies S_CG = Σ_i S_i + O(|Λ|/ℓ^d e^{-ℓ/ξ}), where ℓ ≫ ξ is the cell diameter. The correction is exponentially suppressed per cell, making entropy additive and recovering the Ruelle-Fisher thermodynamic limit. For long-range (non-tempered) interactions, non-additivity is quantified by inter-cell mutual information. Spatial averaging does not commute with nonlinear thermodynamic functionals; a generalized Euler relation with surface corrections is derived.
AI.conclusion: Extensivity is not a necessary postulate but follows from microscopic conditions; its breakdown for long-range interactions is captured by mutual information, and the averaging problem for thermodynamic functionals mirrors the cosmological averaging problem, with explicit surface-term corrections to the Euler relation.

title: Anomalies in the thermal conductivity of honeycomb antiferromagnet MnPS$_{3}$
comment: 25 pages, 11 figures, to appear in PRB
summary: Intrinsic two-dimensional magnets serve as a good platform to explore collective, charge-neutral and low-energy excitations. Distinguishing the crucial role of them in experimental aspect remains a challenge for decades. Here, we study the thermal transport in honeycomb antiferromagnet MnPS$_{3}$ with $T_N$=78 K down to very low temperatures (<0.01$T_N$). At high temperatures (>0.1$T_N$), the field dependence of the thermal Hall conductivity exhibits a linear phonon Hall effect and a peak associated with the spin-flop transition due to a strong spin-lattice coupling, well reproducing the previous report (Phys. Rev. B 110, 165147 (2024)). Notably, below 2 K, we find that the field dependence of the thermal Hall conductivity exhibits sign reversals within the spin-flop phase, at which the field dependence of the longitudinal thermal conductivity also shows multiple valleys. We suggest that these anomalies are caused by the redistribution of Berry curvature in magnon bands, demonstrating the superior performance of the thermal Hall measurements to detect the Berry curvature distributions in magnetic insulators.

AI.tldr: This paper studies thermal transport in the honeycomb antiferromagnet MnPS₃ at very low temperatures (<0.01T_N). At high temperatures, it reproduces known phonon Hall effects and spin-flop transitions. Below 2 K, the thermal Hall conductivity shows sign reversals and the longitudinal conductivity shows multiple valleys within the spin-flop phase, attributed to Berry curvature redistribution in magnon bands.
AI.motivation: To experimentally detect and distinguish the role of low-energy collective excitations (magnons) in intrinsic two-dimensional magnets, a challenge that has persisted for decades.
AI.method: Thermal transport measurements (thermal Hall conductivity and longitudinal thermal conductivity) on MnPS₃ down to very low temperatures (<0.01T_N ~ 0.78 K), with applied magnetic fields.
AI.result: Below 2 K, the thermal Hall conductivity exhibits sign reversals within the spin-flop phase, and the longitudinal thermal conductivity shows multiple valleys, both not observed in previous higher-temperature studies.
AI.conclusion: These low-temperature anomalies arise from redistribution of Berry curvature in magnon bands, demonstrating that thermal Hall measurements are a superior probe for detecting Berry curvature distributions in magnetic insulators.

title: Localization of a quantum particle in a classical one-component plasma. II. Dynamic Disorder and Temporal Decorrelation
summary: We extend the static theory of disorder-induced exponential decay of the averaged Green function of a quantum charged particle in a classical one-component plasma to the dynamic regime by incorporating the temporal evolution of the ionic density fluctuations within the random phase approximation. The dynamic potential correlator is derived from the fluctuation-dissipation theorem and the Kramers--Kronig relations. Within the eikonal (straight-line) approximation, the effective disorder strength is expressed through the dielectric function of the ion plasma. For particles moving faster than the ion thermal speed, the static Coulomb logarithm is recovered, with the large-distance cutoff replaced by the dynamic scale $v/ω_{pi}$. For slow particles, the Coulomb logarithm disappears completely and the disorder strength becomes proportional to the velocity, leading to a fundamentally different scaling of the localization length. In particular, the strong-disorder length diverges as $k^{-1/3}$ for $v\ll v_{\mathrm{th}}$, whereas it saturates in the static limit, indicating that ultra-slow particles are not exponentially localized in a dynamic plasma. A crossover between the quasi-static and dynamic regimes occurs when the particle speed becomes comparable to the ion thermal speed.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the static theory of disorder-induced exponential decay of the averaged Green function for a quantum charged particle in a classical one-component plasma to the dynamic regime, using the random phase approximation to incorporate temporal ionic density fluctuations. Key findings include: fast particles recover static Coulomb logarithm with a dynamic cutoff; slow particles lose the Coulomb logarithm entirely, with disorder strength scaling linearly with velocity; ultra-slow particles are not exponentially localized (localization length diverges as k^{-1/3}), in contrast to the static saturation.
AI.motivation: To extend the static theory of disorder-induced exponential localization of a quantum charged particle in a classical plasma to the dynamic regime by accounting for time-dependent ionic density fluctuations.
AI.method: The dynamic potential correlator is derived from the fluctuation-dissipation theorem and Kramers-Kronig relations. Within the eikonal (straight-line) approximation, the effective disorder strength is expressed through the dielectric function of the ion plasma.
AI.result: For fast particles (v > v_th), static Coulomb logarithm is recovered with dynamic cutoff v/ω_pi. For slow particles (v << v_th), Coulomb logarithm vanishes; disorder strength scales with velocity; strong-disorder length diverges as k^{-1/3}, indicating no exponential localization for ultra-slow particles in dynamic plasma.
AI.conclusion: A crossover between quasi-static and dynamic regimes occurs when particle speed becomes comparable to ion thermal speed. Ultra-slow particles are not exponentially localized in a dynamic plasma, unlike in the static limit where localization length saturates.

title: Metal-free heteroatom doping of carbon nitride for enhanced photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide production
summary: The photocatalytic production of hydrogen peroxide (H$_2$O$_2$) from water is a promising strategy for solar-to-chemical energy conversion. Herein, we investigate the effect of metal-free heteroatom doping (B, O, P, and S) on the structural, electronic, and photocatalytic properties of graphitic carbon nitride (C$_3$N$_4$) for H$_2$O$_2$ production under simulated solar irradiation. While pristine C$_3$N$_4$ exhibits stacked nanosheets, doping induces disorder, partial exfoliation, and changes in interlayer spacing, confirming successful heteroatom incorporation and modification of the electronic and optical properties. Photocatalytic experiments reveal that H$_2$O$_2$ production strongly depends on the sacrificial agent, pH, and reactive-species scavengers. All doped catalysts show enhanced activity compared to pristine C$_3$N$_4$, with 9.6-, 14.8-, 11.0-, and 16.4-fold increases for B-, P-, O-, and S-doped C$_3$N$_4$, respectively. S-doped C$_3$N$_4$ achieved the highest H$_2$O$_2$ production rate of 3022.1 $μ$mol h$^{-1}$ g$^{-1}$ and an apparent quantum yield of 8.1\%, attributed to improved charge separation and optimized selectivity. Mechanistic studies indicate that oxygen activation mainly follows a two-electron (2e$^{-}$) pathway driven by charge-carrier modulation and reactive oxygen species dynamics, with singlet oxygen and photogenerated holes playing a dominant role. In addition, S-doped C$_3$N$_4$ retained over 95\% of its activity after five cycles. These results highlight metal-free heteroatom doping as an effective strategy for sustainable photocatalytic H$_2$O$_2$ generation.

AI.tldr: This study investigates metal-free heteroatom doping (B, O, P, S) of graphitic carbon nitride (C₃N₄) for photocatalytic H₂O₂ production. S-doped C₃N₄ achieves the best performance (3022.1 μmol h⁻¹ g⁻¹, 8.1% AQY), with 16.4-fold enhancement over pristine C₃N₄, attributed to improved charge separation and a two-electron oxygen reduction pathway.
AI.motivation: To develop an efficient, sustainable, and metal-free photocatalyst for solar-driven hydrogen peroxide production from water, addressing the need for clean solar-to-chemical energy conversion.
AI.method: Metal-free heteroatom doping (B, O, P, S) of graphitic carbon nitride (C₃N₄); characterized structural and electronic changes; evaluated photocatalytic H₂O₂ production under simulated solar irradiation with varying sacrificial agents, pH, and scavengers.
AI.result: All doped catalysts outperformed pristine C₃N₄: 9.6× (B), 14.8× (P), 11.0× (O), and 16.4× (S) enhancement. S-doped C₃N₄ achieved 3022.1 μmol h⁻¹ g⁻¹ H₂O₂ production rate and 8.1% apparent quantum yield, with >95% activity retention after five cycles.
AI.conclusion: Metal-free heteroatom doping is an effective strategy for enhancing photocatalytic H₂O₂ generation. S-doping yields the best performance via improved charge separation and a two-electron oxygen reduction pathway dominated by singlet oxygen and photogenerated holes.

title: Indicators for phonon hydrodynamics from first principles predictions of thermal conductivity
summary: Hydrodynamic heat flow, where out-of-equilibrium phonons collectively drift in response to an applied temperature differential, has attracted renewed interest following its experimental observation in graphite at temperatures as high as 300 K. To accelerate discovery of material alternatives to graphite and suitable experimental conditions for realizing this non-Fourier heat flow regime, computationally efficient indicators derived from predictive first principles approaches are necessary. Here we show that the ratio of thermal conductivity ($κ$) obtained from the complete solution of the linearized Peierls-Boltzmann equation (LPBE) for phonon transport ($κ_{LPBE}$), to that from the relaxation time approximation (RTA) for phonon decay ($κ_{RTA}$), is a low cost indicator for phonon hydrodynamics. We show that collectively drifting non-equilibrium phonons amplify the ratio of $κ_{LPBE}$ to $κ_{RTA}$, while a small $κ_{LPBE}/κ_{RTA}$ correlates with predominantly diffusive phonon transport. On the other hand, we find that conventional approaches that rely only on momentum-conserving Normal and momentum-dissipating Umklapp scattering rates, such as the RTA and the Callaway approximations to the LPBE, are inadequate to predict phonon hydrodynamics. Furthermore, our study reveals that the indicator ratio - $κ_{LPBE}/κ_{RTA}$, and therefore the strength of hydrodynamic signatures, decrease with increasing Brillouin zone (BZ) sampling density for several ultrahigh-$κ$ materials at low temperatures, thus underscoring the need for careful BZ sampling convergence studies to ensure robust predictions of phonon hydrodynamics. This computationally inexpensive indicator of phonon hydrodynamics will accelerate the search for new materials that exhibit such unconventional heat flow regimes.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes that the ratio κ_LPBE/κ_RTA (thermal conductivity from the full Peierls-Boltzmann equation vs. relaxation time approximation) serves as a computationally efficient indicator for identifying phonon hydrodynamic heat flow in materials, outperforming conventional approaches based solely on Normal vs. Umklapp scattering rates.
AI.motivation: To accelerate discovery of material alternatives to graphite and suitable experimental conditions for realizing non-Fourier (hydrodynamic) heat flow, computationally efficient indicators derived from predictive first-principles approaches are needed.
AI.method: The authors show that the ratio of thermal conductivity from the full linearized Peierls-Boltzmann equation (κ_LPBE) to that from the relaxation time approximation (κ_RTA) is a low-cost indicator for phonon hydrodynamics. They compare this against conventional approaches (RTA and Callaway approximations) and study the effect of Brillouin zone sampling density.
AI.result: Collectively drifting non-equilibrium phonons amplify κ_LPBE/κ_RTA, while a small ratio correlates with diffusive transport. Conventional scattering-rate-based approaches (RTA, Callaway) are inadequate for predicting hydrodynamics. The ratio decreases with increasing BZ sampling density for several ultrahigh-κ materials at low temperatures, highlighting the need for careful convergence studies.
AI.conclusion: The κ_LPBE/κ_RTA ratio is a computationally inexpensive and effective indicator of phonon hydrodynamics that will accelerate the search for new materials exhibiting unconventional heat flow.

title: Ordering, correlation functions and phase transitions in molecular systems
summary: Although the classical density functional theory (DFT) of inhomogeneous fluids was formulated more than four decades ago, its application to broken symmetry phases of molecular systems remained a challenge. Approximate free energy functionals proposed in the past failed to give accurate description of relative stability of phases, phase transitions, and of properties arising due to broken symmetry. In a DFT pair correlation functions (PCFs) play a fundamental role. While in the case of homogeneous fluids, PCFs are routinely determined using experimental, theoretical or simulation methods, determination of PCFs of broken symmetry phases remained a problem. Breaking of symmetry at the transition point gives rise a new contribution to correlation functions which may differ significantly from that of the coexisting higher symmetry phase. We review methods which have been developed in the last few years to calculate PCFs of broken symmetry phases and their inclusion in the expressions of the grand potential and the intrinsic free-energy. This leads to formulation of an exact DFT. We describe application of the theory to freezing of variety of fluids into ordered phases and transition from an ordered phase of higher symmetry to a phase of lower symmetry. Comparison of results found from different versions of DFT and simulations reveal their accuracy. A brief description of basics of statistical mechanics is included to make the article self-contained.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews recent developments in density functional theory (DFT) for calculating pair correlation functions (PCFs) in broken symmetry phases, leading to an exact DFT formulation. It covers applications to freezing transitions and symmetry-breaking phase transitions, with validation against simulations.
AI.motivation: Classical DFT of inhomogeneous fluids, despite being formulated decades ago, has struggled to accurately describe broken symmetry phases in molecular systems due to failures of approximate free energy functionals in predicting phase stability, transitions, and broken-symmetry properties.
AI.method: The authors review methods developed in recent years to calculate pair correlation functions (PCFs) of broken symmetry phases and incorporate them into the grand potential and intrinsic free-energy expressions, leading to an exact DFT formulation.
AI.result: The exact DFT with properly included PCFs yields accurate descriptions of freezing transitions from fluids into ordered phases and transitions between ordered phases of different symmetries. Results from various DFT versions compare favorably with simulations.
AI.conclusion: The inclusion of broken-symmetry PCFs in DFT provides a rigorous framework for studying phase transitions involving symmetry breaking, with accuracy validated against simulation data.

title: Localization of a quantum particle in a classical one-component plasma.III. Mutual coherence and coherence degradation in Coulomb-disordered media
summary: We derive the mutual coherence function of an electron beam propagating through a static or dynamic Coulomb-disordered medium and show that its decay introduces an intrinsic coherence-reduction mechanism relevant for electron microscopy in Coulomb-disordered media. Using the Efimov path-integral formalism, the coherence length $ρ_c$ is expressed through the same disorder correlator that governs the single-particle localization length $\ell$. For both a static electrolyte and a dynamic plasma we obtain a universal relation $ρ_c \sim λ_D \sqrt{\ell/L}$, where $λ_D$ is the Debye length and $L$ the sample thickness. In the static case $\ell\propto k^{2}$ (electron momentum), whereas in the dynamic slow-particle regime $\ell\propto k$, leading to qualitatively different energy dependences of the coherence scale. The ion thermal velocity cancels out in the final expression, demonstrating a formal connection between transverse coherence decay and longitudinal localization phenomena. Exact analytical results are given for the phase structure function of a model electrolyte, and numerical estimates indicate that disorder-induced phase decorrelation may contribute appreciably to the attenuation of high-spatial-frequency contrast under experimentally relevant liquid-cell electron microscopy conditions. Possible implications for cryo-EM, disordered liquids, soft condensed matter, and biological media are discussed. In an appendix we extend the theory to the relativistic regime relevant for transmission electron microscopy.

AI.tldr: This paper derives the mutual coherence function of an electron beam in Coulomb-disordered media, establishing a universal relation between coherence length, Debye length, sample thickness, and localization length, with implications for electron microscopy in liquids and biological media.
AI.motivation: To understand and quantify how Coulomb disorder (from static electrolytes or dynamic plasmas) intrinsically degrades electron beam coherence in electron microscopy, and to connect this coherence decay to single-particle localization phenomena.
AI.method: Efimov path-integral formalism; derivation of mutual coherence function and coherence length via disorder correlator; analytical results for phase structure function of a model electrolyte; extension to relativistic regime in appendix.
AI.result: Universal relation ρ_c ∼ λ_D √(ℓ/L); static case ℓ ∝ k², dynamic slow-particle regime ℓ ∝ k; ion thermal velocity cancels; disorder-induced phase decorrelation can attenuate high-spatial-frequency contrast in liquid-cell electron microscopy.
AI.conclusion: Disorder-induced coherence loss is a measurable and potentially significant effect in electron microscopy of Coulomb-disordered media, with implications for cryo-EM, disordered liquids, soft condensed matter, and biological samples.

title: Chemo-mechanical coupling stabilizes mixed $\mathrm{Ag}_{x}\mathrm{Cu}_{1-x}\mathrm{GaSe}_{2}$ solar-cell absorbers: Insights from Monte-Carlo simulations assisted by ab initio informed machine-learning potentials
summary: Alloying Ag into Cu(In,Ga)Se$_2$ has enabled record solar-cell efficiencies ($\sim23.6\%$), yet their long-term stability remains in question because initio calculations predict a Ag-Cu miscibility gap near ambient temperature. By off-lattice Monte-Carlo simulations using a newly developed machine learning (ML) interatomic potential we show that the presence of coherency strain is resolving the controversy between experimental observations and the predicted phase stability. Incorporating elastic energy contributions present in a coherent setup results in complete Ag-Cu miscibility, whereas the expected phase separation occurs in the absence of coherency strains with respect to the end boundary phases, which are mimicked by an incoherent interface with misfit dislocations. The developed ML-MC framework provides a novel approach for resolving discrepancies in thermodynamic stability for systems where mechanical and chemical effects compete.

AI.tldr: Using machine-learning interatomic potentials and off-lattice Monte-Carlo simulations, this study resolves the controversy between predicted Ag-Cu miscibility gap and observed complete miscibility in Ag-alloyed CIGS solar cells, showing that coherency strain from lattice mismatch suppresses phase separation.
AI.motivation: To resolve the discrepancy between first-principles predictions of a Ag-Cu miscibility gap in Ag-alloyed Cu(In,Ga)Se₂ solar cells and experimental observations of high-efficiency devices, by investigating the role of coherency strain on thermodynamic phase stability.
AI.method: Off-lattice Monte-Carlo simulations using a newly developed machine learning interatomic potential to model Ag-Cu alloying in CIGS, comparing coherent (strained) vs. incoherent (with misfit dislocations) interfacial conditions.
AI.result: Complete Ag-Cu miscibility is achieved under coherency strain, while phase separation occurs when coherency strains are absent (incoherent interfaces with misfit dislocations).
AI.conclusion: Coherency strain resolves the controversy between predicted thermodynamic instability and observed high-efficiency Ag-alloyed CIGS devices; the ML-MC framework offers a general approach for disentangling competing mechanical and chemical effects in thermodynamic stability.

title: Combinatorial Survey of Structural Phase Distribution and Magnetism in Fe-Ge-Te Composition-spread Thin Film Libraries
summary: Recently, magnetic 2-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) materials have garnered tremendous attention. The vdW ferromagnet Fe5Ge1Te2 has a Curie temperature Tc of ~ 270 K, which is tailorable by tuning the stoichiometry and the Fe deficiency to reach room temperature. To explore the expanded compositional space, we implemented combinatorial synthesis and high-throughput characterization to investigate the structural phase distribution and ferromagnetism of a Fe-Ge-Te thin film library. The library was prepared by magnetron co-sputtering followed by annealing in vacuum or in an inert environment. Composition and structural phase distribution of the 177 pads in the library were characterized using high-throughput wavelength dispersive spectroscopy (WDS), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and two-point probe resistance measurements. We leverage unsupervised machine learning to cluster the XRD dataset into groups of compositions with similar structural phases, and further study the ferromagnetic properties via SQUID magnetometry and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) across different clusters. The results are compared against magnetization and structural models calculated using DFT. Our results demonstrate that the hexagonal crystal structure is a critical prerequisite for ferromagnetism in this system, and that unexplored materials adopting this structure can be efficiently identified as possible ferromagnetic materials using our high-throughput, ML-assisted framework. This workflow based on the combinatorial strategy allows us to rapidly capture the composition-structure-magnetic property map across a broad compositional landscape of novel magnetic materials.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a high-throughput combinatorial synthesis and machine-learning-assisted characterization framework to map composition-structure-magnetic property relationships in Fe-Ge-Te thin film libraries, identifying that the hexagonal crystal structure is essential for ferromagnetism in this system.
AI.motivation: To accelerate discovery of magnetic 2D van der Waals materials by efficiently exploring the expanded compositional space of Fe-Ge-Te, motivated by the tunable room-temperature ferromagnetism in Fe5Ge1Te2.
AI.method: Combinatorial magnetron co-sputtering of Fe-Ge-Te thin film libraries (177 pads), high-throughput WDS, XRD, two-point probe resistance measurements, unsupervised ML clustering of XRD data, SQUID magnetometry and XMCD for magnetic characterization, and DFT calculations for comparison.
AI.result: The hexagonal crystal structure is identified as a critical prerequisite for ferromagnetism; the ML-assisted combinatorial framework efficiently identifies unexplored compositions with this structure as potential ferromagnetic materials.
AI.conclusion: The high-throughput, ML-assisted combinatorial workflow enables rapid mapping of composition-structure-magnetic property relationships across broad compositional landscapes, accelerating discovery of novel magnetic materials.

title: Characterisation of fire-damaged batteries,implications for recycling
summary: As lithium-ion battery demand grows, so do fire safety challenges. Despite this, research on fire-damaged batteries remains limited. This study explores the distribution of valuable metals (such as Ni, Mn, Co, Cu) in two types of waste derived from lithium-ion nickel-manganese-cobalt oxide batteries (NMC811), black mass (BM) and fire-damaged waste (FD). It emphasizes that cobalt, manganese, and nickel-rich NMC811 particles are predominantly found in smaller particle size fractions (<125 microns), where they can account for up to 85 percent of total metal content. Fire-damaged (FD) batteries show a similar, though less pronounced, trend. Evidence of structural degradation suggests that fire temperatures exceeded 500°C; however, the presence of residual organic binders indicates that heat was unevenly distributed during the fire. FD batteries become friable and easily fragment into fine particles, which can hinder the effective separation of copper and aluminium current collectors, increasing their presence in processed material. The inclusion of FD batteries in standard BM processing introduces variability in output composition, potentially lowering the concentration of high-value NMC811 materials present. To maintain product quality and recycling output values, it is recommended that FD batteries are processed separately. Alternatively, particle size separation may allow for tailored outputs aligned with specific customer requirements.

AI.tldr: This study compares the distribution of valuable metals (Ni, Mn, Co, Cu) in black mass and fire-damaged waste from NMC811 batteries. Fire damage causes structural degradation above 500°C, uneven heat distribution, and friability leading to fine particle fragmentation, which complicates metal separation. High-value NMC811 particles concentrate in <125 µm fractions. FD batteries should be processed separately to maintain recycling output quality.
AI.motivation: Despite growing fire safety challenges from increasing lithium-ion battery demand, research on fire-damaged batteries and their recycling implications remains limited.
AI.method: The study analyzes the distribution of valuable metals (Ni, Mn, Co, Cu) in two types of waste from NMC811 batteries: black mass (BM) and fire-damaged waste (FD), examining particle size fractions and structural degradation evidence.
AI.result: NMC811 particles are predominantly found in <125 µm fractions, accounting for up to 85% of total metal content. FD batteries show a similar but less pronounced trend. Fire temperatures exceeded 500°C with uneven heat distribution. FD batteries become friable, fragment into fine particles, hindering current collector separation and increasing impurity presence.
AI.conclusion: FD batteries should be processed separately from standard BM to maintain product quality and recycling output values, or particle size separation can be used for tailored outputs based on customer requirements.

title: High-Density Horizontal Arrays of Single-Chirality Carbon Nanotubes
summary: Highly ordered high-density arrays of single-chirality single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) are greatly desired for exploring the intrinsic anisotropic properties and collective performance of such 1-dimensional (1D) nanomaterials. Here we present a Marangoni flow-induced self-assembly (MISA) strategy to fabricate monolayered SWCNT arrays achieving a packing density of ~200 ${μm}^{-1}$ and a 2-dimensional order parameter ($S_{2\mathrm{D}}$) of ~0.95. Relying on its general compatibility with both organic and aqueous dispersions, we prepare single-chirality and enantiomer-pure SWCNT arrays from organic and aqueous dispersions resulting from the sorting processes. The anisotropic optical and electrical properties of the arrays are demonstrated by the polarization-dependent Rabi splitting as well as polarized near-infrared light emission and detection. With the great tolerance to solutions, substrates, and materials, as well as the feasibility and controllability, MISA shows great potential in the assembly of 1D nanomaterials.

AI.tldr: A Marangoni flow-induced self-assembly (MISA) strategy is developed to fabricate highly ordered, high-density monolayered arrays of single-chirality and enantiomer-pure single-walled carbon nanotubes, achieving a packing density of ~200 μm⁻¹ and a 2D order parameter of ~0.95, with demonstrated anisotropic optical and electrical properties.
AI.motivation: Highly ordered high-density arrays of single-chirality SWCNTs are greatly desired for exploring intrinsic anisotropic properties and collective performance of 1D nanomaterials.
AI.method: Marangoni flow-induced self-assembly (MISA) strategy to fabricate monolayered SWCNT arrays, compatible with both organic and aqueous dispersions from sorting processes.
AI.result: Achieved packing density of ~200 μm⁻¹ and 2D order parameter (S₂D) of ~0.95; demonstrated polarization-dependent Rabi splitting and polarized near-infrared light emission and detection.
AI.conclusion: MISA shows great potential in the assembly of 1D nanomaterials due to its tolerance to solutions, substrates, and materials, as well as its feasibility and controllability.

title: First-principles investigation of small polarons in rhombohedral NaNbO$_{3}$
summary: Sodium niobate (NaNbO$_{3}$) is a perovskite oxide and a key component of emerging lead-free antiferroelectric capacitors for high-energy-density applications. However, its performance can be hindered by irreversible phase transitions and leakage currents associated with low electrical resistivity. Defect and doping engineering offers a potential way to overcome these problems, but its use requires a detailed understanding of electronic, ionic, and polaron charge-compensation mechanisms, where the role of polarons remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigate the stability of small hole and electron polarons in rhombohedral NaNbO$_{3}$, which is a structurally well-defined model system that avoids lattice-dynamical instabilities. Trapping energies are calculated using density-functional theory corrected by a Hubbard $U$, using the enforced-piecewise-linearity approach including finite-size scaling. For the small hole-polaron centered on O-2$p$ orbital, we find a trapping energy of $-$0.65 (eV) and an adiabatic migration barrier of 0.32 (eV) determined by nudged-elastic-band calculations. In contrast, we show that excess electrons do not self-trap on Nb-4$d$ orbitals, reflecting weak electron-phonon coupling in the conduction band manifold. These results identify oxygen as an intrinsic hole trap in NaNbO$_{3}$ and highlight the importance of including hole polarons in defect models of NaNbO$_{3}$-based electroceramics.

AI.tldr: This study uses DFT+U calculations to investigate small hole and electron polarons in rhombohedral NaNbO₃, finding that holes self-trap on oxygen with a trapping energy of -0.65 eV and migration barrier of 0.32 eV, while excess electrons do not self-trap on Nb-4d orbitals, highlighting the importance of hole polarons in defect models for NaNbO₃-based electroceramics.
AI.motivation: To address the performance limitations of NaNbO₃ (irreversible phase transitions and leakage currents due to low electrical resistivity) by understanding the electronic, ionic, and polaron charge-compensation mechanisms, particularly the largely unexplored role of polarons.
AI.method: Density-functional theory corrected by a Hubbard U (DFT+U) with enforced-piecewise-linearity approach and finite-size scaling, plus nudged-elastic-band calculations for migration barriers.
AI.result: Hole polarons self-trap on O-2p orbitals with a trapping energy of -0.65 eV and adiabatic migration barrier of 0.32 eV; excess electrons do not self-trap on Nb-4d orbitals due to weak electron-phonon coupling.
AI.conclusion: Oxygen acts as an intrinsic hole trap in NaNbO₃, and hole polarons must be included in defect models of NaNbO₃-based electroceramics.

title: Short-range order in the CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy from cluster expansion
summary: We investigate the short-range order (SRO) and phase stability of the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy using cluster expansion supplemented by an eigen-decomposition analysis of the SRO parameters. Our results reveal that the primary ordering behavior is determined by strong Cr-Cr repulsive interactions, complemented by attractive heteroatomic Cr-$X$ pairs in the first nearest-neighbor shell. This chemical affinity is consistent with the emergence of ordered local environments and appears to be a major contributor to the primary order-disorder transition. At lower temperatures, the spectral SRO analysis suggests two additional lower-temperature instabilities: a collective ordering instability and an Fe-rich local clustering instability.

AI.tldr: Cr-Cr repulsion drives short-range order in CoCrFeMnNi, with Cr-X attraction creating ordered environments; lower temperatures reveal additional ordering and Fe-clustering instabilities.
AI.motivation: To understand the short-range order and phase stability in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy.
AI.method: Cluster expansion with eigen-decomposition analysis of SRO parameters.
AI.result: Cr-Cr repulsive interactions dominate ordering, with attractive Cr-X pairs in first NN shell; additional ordering and Fe-rich clustering instabilities appear at lower temperatures.
AI.conclusion: Chemical affinity via Cr-X pairs is the major contributor to the order-disorder transition in this HEA.

title: Why hole polaron formation on oxygen is limiting the Fermi level in Fe acceptor doped BaTiO$_{3}$ under oxidizing conditions
summary: Oxidizing Fe-doped BaTiO$_3$ is commonly expected to convert substitutional Fe$^{3+}$ acceptors into formal Fe$^{4+}$ centers. Yet, the experimentally accessible picture based on electron-paramagnetic resonance (EPR) is dominated by Fe$^{3+}$-related signatures, while Fe$^{4+}$ is not a straightforward observable. Here we show that this apparent discrepancy reflects the preferred location of the oxidizing hole: not on Fe, but on oxygen. Using density-functional theory with with occupation-matrix control and a piecewise-linearity-based Hubbard correction (DFT+$U$) for O-2$p$ states, we find that an oxygen-centered hole polaron is forming a Fe$^{3+}$-O$^{-}$ complex that is lower in energy than the formal Fe$^{4+}$ configuration. Our results identify ligand-hole formation as a favorable charge-compensation mechanism in oxidized Fe-doped BaTiO$_3$ and provide an explanation for the predominance of Fe$^{3+}$-based centers in spectroscopy. More broadly, they show how oxygen polarons can limit Fermi-level shifts and control the electronic response of acceptor-doped ferroelectric perovskites.

AI.tldr: In Fe-doped BaTiO₃, oxidation does not produce Fe⁴⁺ as expected; instead, an oxygen hole polaron forms a Fe³⁺-O⁻ complex, explaining the dominance of Fe³⁺ EPR signals and revealing ligand-hole formation as the key charge-compensation mechanism.
AI.motivation: To resolve the experimental discrepancy where oxidized Fe-doped BaTiO₃ shows Fe³⁺-dominated EPR signals rather than the expected Fe⁴⁺, by uncovering the true charge compensation mechanism.
AI.method: DFT+U with occupation-matrix control and piecewise-linearity-based Hubbard correction on O-2p states.
AI.result: The oxygen-centered hole polaron (Fe³⁺-O⁻ complex) is energetically more favorable than the formal Fe⁴⁺ configuration.
AI.conclusion: Ligand-hole formation is the preferred charge-compensation mechanism in oxidized Fe-doped BaTiO₃, explaining Fe³⁺ spectroscopic predominance and showing oxygen polarons limit Fermi-level shifts in acceptor-doped ferroelectric perovskites.

title: Tuning the Charge Transfer of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides via Misfit Layer Compounds
summary: Misfit layer compounds (MLCs) are a versatile platform for exploring the electronic phase diagram of two dimensional (2D) materials beyond the limits of conventional gating techniques. This work demonstrates the precise tunability of electron doping in NbSe2 monolayers through chemical alloying within the rocksalt layer of (LaxPb1xSe)1.14(NbSe2)2 heterostructures. By combining first principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations with angle resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), we prove that the rocksalt unit acts as an universal electron donor. We show that varying the La Pb ratio results in a rigid Fermi level shift, still preserving the NbSe2 electronic structure. Crucially, photon energy dependent ARPES confirms that the NbSe2 layers nearly maintain their intrinsic 2D character and orbital identity within the three dimensional misfit. This study establishes MLCs as a reliable platform for engineering emergent states in 2D transition metal dichalcogenides through precise stoichiometric control.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that misfit layer compounds (MLCs) with (LaxPb1-xSe)1.14(NbSe2)2 heterostructures allow precise electron doping control in NbSe2 monolayers by tuning the La/Pb ratio in the rocksalt layer, which acts as a universal electron donor without altering the NbSe2 electronic structure or its 2D character.
AI.motivation: To explore beyond conventional gating techniques for tuning electronic properties of 2D materials, specifically to demonstrate precise electron doping control in NbSe2 monolayers using misfit layer compounds.
AI.method: Combined first-principles DFT calculations with angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), including photon energy dependent ARPES to verify 2D character, on (LaxPb1-xSe)1.14(NbSe2)2 heterostructures with varying La/Pb ratios.
AI.result: Varying the La/Pb ratio produces a rigid Fermi level shift while preserving the NbSe2 electronic structure; the rocksalt unit acts as a universal electron donor; NbSe2 layers maintain their intrinsic 2D character and orbital identity within the 3D misfit structure.
AI.conclusion: MLCs are a reliable platform for engineering emergent electronic states in 2D transition metal dichalcogenides through precise stoichiometric control via chemical alloying.

title: Metastable Cu$_{1-x}$CrTe$_2$ -- Completing the copper chromium delafossite series through soft chemistry
summary: In the layered copper chromium dichalcogenide series CuCr$X_2$, the oxide, the sulfide, and the selenide analogues have been reported, but the telluride CuCrTe$_2$ has remained unsynthesized so far. Here, we report the synthesis of Cu$_{1-x}$CrTe$_2$ ($x \approx 0.3$), which forms only within a narrow temperature window near 90 °C by solvothermal cation exchange of K$_{1-x}$CrTe$_2$ ($x \approx 0.3$) and CuBr. Cu$_{1-x}$CrTe$_2$ undergoes a magnetostructural transition to an antiferromagnetic state at $T_\mathrm{N}=239$ K, a Néel temperature that is high relative to other $A$CrTe$_2$ phases and comparable to that of ferromagnetic, fully-deintercalated CrTe$_2$. Cu$_{1-x}$CrTe$_2$ is metastable and decomposes at temperatures as low as 250 °C to form spinel CuCr$_2$Te$_4$. These results highlight the importance of low-temperature topochemical routes for accessing metastable Cu(I)-containing tellurides that are inaccessible by conventional solid-state synthesis.

AI.tldr: The paper reports the first synthesis of Cu-deficient Cu₁₋ₓCrTe₂ (x≈0.3) via low-temperature solvothermal cation exchange at ~90°C. It exhibits a magnetostructural transition to antiferromagnetism at TN=239 K—high for ACrTe₂ phases—and decomposes to spinel CuCr₂Te₄ above 250°C, demonstrating the utility of low-temperature topochemical routes for metastable tellurides.
AI.motivation: The telluride analogue CuCrTe₂ in the layered CuCrX₂ series had remained unsynthesized, motivating the search for a viable synthetic route.
AI.method: Solvothermal cation exchange of K₁₋ₓCrTe₂ (x≈0.3) with CuBr at ~90°C within a narrow temperature window.
AI.result: Synthesis of metastable Cu₁₋ₓCrTe₂ (x≈0.3) which exhibits an antiferromagnetic transition at TN=239 K and decomposes to spinel CuCr₂Te₄ above 250°C.
AI.conclusion: Low-temperature topochemical routes are essential for accessing metastable Cu(I)-containing tellurides that cannot be obtained via conventional solid-state synthesis.

title: Epitaxial growth and magnetic phase transitions in non-centrosymmetric EuPdSi$_3$ thin films
summary: Non-centrosymmetric magnetic materials are a promising platform for stabilizing chiral spin textures, such as skyrmions and cycloidal magnetic states. This is particularly true in epitaxial thin film geometries, where strain and interface effects offer additional control. Herein, we report on the first epitaxial thin films of EuPdSi$_3$ grown by molecular beam epitaxy on MgO(001). X-ray diffraction confirms an epitaxial relationship of tetragonal EuPdSi$_3$ in the BaNiSn$_3$ structure with out-of-plane c-axis orientation and parallel in-plane a-axes. Hard x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals a stable Eu valence of 2.0, yielding a large magnetic moment of approximately 7 $μ_B$ per Eu atom in accordance with Hund's rule. Owing to the non-centrosymmetric crystal structure, non-collinear magnetic states such as Néel-type skyrmions and cycloidal phases are allowed by symmetry. Electronic transport measurements reveal two magnetic phase transitions at 19 K and 15 K in zero applied field. Under magnetic fields applied along the crystallographic [100] and [001] directions, distinct temperature dependent magnetic phases emerge, demonstrating the sensitivity of the magnetic ground state to field orientation in epitaxial EuPdSi$_3$ thin films.

AI.tldr: First epitaxial thin films of EuPdSi₃ grown on MgO(001) via MBE exhibit stable Eu²⁺ valence (7 μB/Eu), non-centrosymmetric tetragonal BaNiSn₃ structure, and two magnetic phase transitions (19 K and 15 K) with field-orientation-dependent magnetic ground states, enabling Néel-type skyrmions and cycloidal phases.
AI.motivation: Non-centrosymmetric magnetic materials are promising for stabilizing chiral spin textures (skyrmions, cycloidal states), especially in epitaxial thin films where strain and interface effects provide additional control. However, EuPdSi₃ had not been explored in thin-film form prior to this work.
AI.method: Epitaxial thin films of EuPdSi₃ were grown by molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) on MgO(001). Characterization included X-ray diffraction for epitaxial relationship, hard X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (HAXPES) for valence state, and electronic transport measurements under magnetic fields along [100] and [001] directions.
AI.result: Tetragonal EuPdSi₃ with BaNiSn₃ structure, out-of-plane c-axis orientation, and parallel in-plane a-axes. Eu valence of 2.0 with ~7 μB magnetic moment per Eu atom. Two zero-field magnetic transitions at 19 K and 15 K. Distinct temperature-dependent magnetic phases emerge under field applied along [100] vs [001].
AI.conclusion: Epitaxial EuPdSi₃ thin films exhibit non-centrosymmetric symmetry allowing Néel-type skyrmions and cycloidal phases, with magnetic ground states highly sensitive to field orientation. This establishes EuPdSi₃ as a candidate for studying chiral spin textures in thin-film form.

title: Spatially-Localized Second Harmonic Generation via Spin Wave Concentration in Patterned YIG Structures
summary:
The anisotropic dispersion and inherent nonlinearity of magnetostatic spin waves in thin films and confined structures provide unique opportunities for implementation in next-generation magnonic devices for data and signal processing. A particular challenge is to establish an effective means to locally generate higher harmonics and subsequently exploit them while avoiding extraneous nonlinear losses.
  Here we demonstrate that deterministically and locally tuning the dispersion relation by geometric confinement through standard patterning processes, allows the creation spatially localized, high-intensity magnons hundreds of $μm$ or even further from the excitation source. The local intensity obtained in passive, lithographically patterned YIG funnel structures is sufficient to achieve second harmonic generation in localized regions via conventional magnon scattering processes. We verify these effects are truly nonlinear processes by direct measurement and comparison of the 1-$ω$ and 2-$ω$ magnon signals as determined by highly sensitive frequency- and spatially-resolved SNS-MOKE technique. This lays the foundation for using similar devices in future magnon-based infrastructures to localize and enhance sensitivity of readout, downstream magnon-based logic operations, and for other higher harmonic generation-related phenomena and low-power magnonics applications.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that geometrically confined YIG funnel structures can locally enhance nonlinear magnon scattering, enabling second harmonic generation far from the excitation source, as verified by SNS-MOKE measurements.
AI.motivation: To establish an effective means to locally generate higher harmonics in magnonic devices while avoiding extraneous nonlinear losses, enabling next-generation data and signal processing.
AI.method: Passive, lithographically patterned YIG funnel structures are used to geometrically tune the dispersion relation via confinement. Second harmonic generation is achieved via conventional magnon scattering, and signals are measured using frequency- and spatially-resolved SNS-MOKE.
AI.result: Local tuning of dispersion via geometric confinement creates spatially localized, high-intensity magnons hundreds of μm from the excitation source, sufficient for second harmonic generation. Nonlinearity is confirmed by comparing 1-ω and 2-ω magnon signals.
AI.conclusion: This approach lays the foundation for magnon-based logic, enhanced readout sensitivity, higher harmonic generation, and low-power magnonics applications.

title: Termination-Preserved Ultra-high Tunneling Magnetoresistance in Altermagnetic KV2Se2O
summary: Altermagnets exhibit nonrelativistic spin splitting without net magnetization, establishing a new platform for next-generation spintronic devices. Although altermagnetic tunnel junctions (AMTJs) represent the most promising realizations, their practical applications are hindered by low tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) ratios and strong sensitivity to interfacial configurations. Here, we systematically explore the transport properties and microscopic mechanisms of AMTJs based on the recently discovered d-wave altermagnet KV2Se2O. Using first-principles calculations and orbital-resolved analysis, we demonstrate that the synergy between compressed nodal-point like spin-degenerate channels and coplanar interfacial magnetic order yields an ultra-high intrinsic TMR above 105% for all interfacial terminations. More importantly, K-termination effectively preserves bulk spin polarization through its unique passivation characteristics, leading to an ultra-high TMR up to 1012%. These results identify the coupling between momentum-space topology and interfacial passivation provides a reliable strategy for realizing giant magnetoresistive responses in altermagnetic spintronic devices.

AI.tldr: The paper explores altermagnetic tunnel junctions (AMTJs) based on d-wave altermagnet KV2Se2O, demonstrating through first-principles calculations that coupling compressed nodal-point spin-degenerate channels with coplanar interfacial magnetic order yields ultra-high TMR ratios exceeding 105% for all interfaces, and up to 1012% with K-termination due to passivation preserving bulk spin polarization.
AI.motivation: Altermagnetic tunnel junctions (AMTJs) are promising for next-generation spintronics but suffer from low TMR ratios and strong sensitivity to interfacial configurations, hindering practical applications.
AI.method: First-principles calculations and orbital-resolved analysis of AMTJs based on d-wave altermagnet KV2Se2O, examining transport properties and microscopic mechanisms across different interfacial terminations.
AI.result: Synergy between compressed nodal-point spin-degenerate channels and coplanar interfacial magnetic order yields ultra-high intrinsic TMR above 105% for all interfacial terminations; K-termination achieves ultra-high TMR up to 1012%.
AI.conclusion: Coupling momentum-space topology with interfacial passivation provides a reliable strategy for realizing giant magnetoresistive responses in altermagnetic spintronic devices.

title: Defect Control via Cu Enrichment Enhances Multifunctional Properties in the Polar Semiconductor Cu1+xMn1-ySiTe3
summary: Polar materials have recently attracted significant interest due to their rich multifunctional properties. The chalcogenide polar semiconductor Cu1-xMn1+ySiTe3 (Cu-deficient) is an emerging multiferroic system in which electric polarization is coupled to magnetization. However, its macroscopic ferroelectric polarization is strongly suppressed due to the presence of a high density of stacking faults. In this work, we demonstrate that these crystal defects, likely originating from non-stoichiometry, can be substantially reduced by increasing the Cu content. Cu-enriched samples, Cu1+xMn1-ySiTe3, crystallize in a noncentrosymmetric monoclinic structure (space group Pm) as the Cu-deficient counterpart but show a nearly stacking-fault-free phase, which is attributed to the emergence of an interstitial site. Consequently, the Cu-enriched samples show a pronounced enhancement of the second-harmonic generation (SHG) response compared to Cu-deficient compositions. Magnetically, the Cu-enriched crystals retain long-range antiferromagnetic order with a Neel temperature of TN ~ 33 K without a glassy state but manifest a distinct spin-flop transition along the polar b-axis that is absent in the Cu-deficient compositions. Furthermore, the electronic ground state evolves from insulating to doped semiconducting behavior upon Cu enrichment. Together, these results establish this material system as a unique and versatile platform for elucidating the interplay among composition, crystal defects, and multifunctional properties, offering a route to design magnetic polar systems with tunable quantum functionalities.

AI.tldr: Cu enrichment in Cu1+xMn1-ySiTe3 reduces stacking faults, enhances SHG response, induces a spin-flop transition along the polar b-axis, and shifts electronic behavior from insulating to doped semiconducting, establishing a tunable platform for multifunctional magnetic polar materials.
AI.motivation: Polar materials attract interest for multifunctional properties, but the ferroelectric polarization in Cu1-xMn1+ySiTe3 is suppressed by high-density stacking faults. The authors aim to reduce these defects to unlock the material's full potential.
AI.method: Cu enrichment (Cu1+xMn1-ySiTe3) is used to introduce an interstitial site, reducing stacking faults. Structural, optical (SHG), magnetic, and electronic transport characterization is performed to compare Cu-deficient and Cu-enriched compositions.
AI.result: Cu-enriched samples show nearly stacking-fault-free phase, enhanced SHG response, long-range antiferromagnetic order (TN ~ 33 K) with a spin-flop transition along the b-axis absent in Cu-deficient samples, and a shift from insulating to doped semiconducting behavior.
AI.conclusion: The Cu-enriched composition provides a versatile platform for studying the interplay of composition, defects, and multifunctional properties, enabling design of magnetic polar systems with tunable quantum functionalities.
